map.An Axiom City episode — Lessons 2-1 & 2-: An Axiom City episode. Lessons 2-1 & 2-2 in one sitting, with three reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected, crew. It is: Pattern distortion found, crew. It is shaped like a clipboard.
map.Previously: on a rained-out field day, f: Before: on a rained-out field day, four sixth graders opened Ada Vex's sealed journal in the old Vexhall Observatory. They woke VEX, a piece of her Pattern Engine. Now the city's patterns are their problem.
map.Founders Festival, day one. Morning. A f: Founders Festival, day one. Morning. A fresh poster, still warm from the census office printer.
map.By order of the census office: the OFFIC: By order of the census office: the OFFICIAL festival census form. Answer it. Do not question it.
It's a form made of questions, Mr. Pimm. Questioning it is the whole point.
map.Distortion source confirmed: the form it: Distortion source found: the form itself. Its questions cannot measure anything real. Crew, read the machine before it reads you.
map.Under the notice board. Theo has been sq: Under the notice board. Theo has been squinting for three whole minutes.
map.Half of these questions could be answere: Half of these questions could be answered by a sign. "What time does the parade start?" Ask a hundred visitors and you get ONE answer. That is a fact lookup.
map.But \"How many napkins does each visitor: But "How many napkins does each visitor grab?" Everybody is different. THAT one would really measure something.
map.Definition loaded: a statistical questio: Word loaded: a statistical question expects answers that VARY. Different people give different answers. A one-answer question is just a fact with a question mark.
map.A statistical question anticipates varie: A statistical question expects many different answers. "How many napkins does each visitor grab?" has many answers. "What time does the parade start?" has exactly one.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. S: Reader, you are our fifth crew member. Sort Pimm's form. Which questions can really measure this festival?
map.Four questions from Pimm's official form: Four questions from Pimm's official form. Tag each one: STATISTICAL (answers vary) or ONE ANSWER (a single fact).
map.Conceptual: a statistical question antic: Conceptual: a statistical question expects many different answers. Ask it to 100 visitors and you get many answers. A fact question gets the same answer no matter who you ask.
map.Procedural: test each line — 'Would two: Procedural: test each line. 'Would two different visitors give two different answers?' What each visitor buys or how long each one waits changes from person to person. A founding year and a count of entrances never change.
map.Harbor Row, mid-morning. Lines everywher: Harbor Row, mid-morning. Lines everywhere. Dev has a stopwatch and a mission.
map.Side quest complete: I timed how long ei: Side quest done: I timed how long eighteen visitors waited in line. Eighteen data points. Raw loot.
map.Raw numbers are mush. I could build that: Raw numbers are mush. I could build them into bars. A histogram.
map.Histogram schema: sort data into equal i: Histogram plan: sort data into equal intervals (bins). Each bar's height = the frequency. That is how many values land in that bin. Bars touch. No gaps.
map.A histogram shows how often data falls i: A histogram shows how often data falls in each interval. Height = frequency. The bars touch because the intervals do.
map.Bar heights, reader — stack the eighteen: Bar heights, reader. Stack the eighteen waits into something Pimm can't argue with!
map.Dev's log — minutes each of 18 visitors:
Dev's log: minutes each of 18 visitors waited in line:
4 · 12 · 25 · 17 · 8 · 21 · 14 · 27 · 11 · 6 · 19 · 23 · 15 · 28 · 13 · 22 · 10 · 20
Count how many waits land in each bin. Then set the three bar heights.
map.Conceptual: each bar's height is a FREQU: Conceptual: each bar's height is a FREQUENCY. It is how many of the 18 waits fall in that interval. Every wait lands in exactly one bin.
map.Procedural: go wait by wait and tick a b: Procedural: go wait by wait and tick a bin: 4→(0–9), 12→(10–19), 25→(20–29)… Your three counts must add up to 18.
map.My churro line is in there somewhere. Lo: My churro line is in there somewhere. Look at it. The festival finally has a shape.
map.Pretty bars, children. But where is the: Pretty bars, children. But where is the TYPICAL wait? Your chart doesn't even list the numbers now!
map.It doesn't have to list them. The bars r: It doesn't have to list them. The bars remember how many. And how many is enough.
map.Pimm produces a rule book. The crew prod: Pimm brings out a rule book. The crew brings better thinking.
map.Observation: ordered readings stack bin: Look: readings in order stack bin by bin. On this demo board, bins of 2, 5 and 3, where is the 5th reading? Bin one holds #1–2. Bin two holds #3–7. The 5th is in bin two.
map.It's a minimap. You don't see every enem: It's a minimap. You don't see every enemy. You see where they gather. Count up the bars and you can find ANY position.
map.Bar heights add up in order: the first b: Bar heights add up in order. The first bar holds the smallest readings. The next bar goes on from there. Adding frequencies left to right finds any position in the data, even with no list.
High noon at the notice board. A crowd. A clerk. A challenge.
map.Eighteen waits, and your precious raw li: Eighteen waits, and your precious raw list is gone. Find me the middle of the line, the 9th and 10th waits, from BARS alone. You can't.
Reader, read the histogram. Call it.
map.Boss Gate: the bins hold 3, then 8, then: Boss Gate: the bins hold 3, then 8, then 7 of the 18 waits. Stack the counts in order and the histogram will show the middle itself.
map.BOSS GATE. Two locks. One smug clerk. (N: BOSS GATE. Two locks. One smug clerk. (No pressure. Some pressure.)
map.Pimm's challenge. Your histogram of 18 w: Pimm's challenge. Your histogram of 18 waits: 0–9 min: 3 waits · 10–19 min: 8 · 20–29 min: 7. The raw list is gone. Two locks:
map.Line the 18 waits up shortest to longest: Line the 18 waits up shortest to longest. Which bin holds the 9th and 10th waits, the middle of the data?
map.How many waits are 10 minutes or more?: How many waits are 10 minutes or more?
map.Conceptual: a histogram remembers HOW MA: Conceptual: a histogram remembers HOW MANY waits are in each interval, in order, shortest bin first. Adding the bar counts left to right shows which interval holds any position: 1st, 9th, 18th.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: the first bar holds: Procedural: Lock 1: the first bar holds waits #1–3. Add the next bar's height to see which positions IT covers. Then check where the 9th and 10th land. Lock 2: add the heights of every bar at 10 minutes or above.
map.The office will… revise the form. With q: The office will… fix the form. With questions that, ahem, vary. Churro, anyone? My treat.
map.One poster down. But a good question onl: One poster down. But a good question only STARTS the data. Somebody still has to find its middle.
map.New distortion humming. It lives in the: New distortion humming. It lives in the exact middle. To be continued…
map.Statistical question.Expects answers tha: Statistical question.Expects answers that vary from person to person. That makes it measurable. A one-answer question is a fact lookup.
map.Histogram.Equal intervals (bins); bar he: Histogram.Equal intervals (bins). Bar height = frequency, how many values land inside. Bars touch because the intervals do.
map.Reading the bars.Frequencies add up in o: Reading the bars.Frequencies add up in order. So stacking bar counts left to right finds any position, even the middle pair, without the raw list.
map.\"A machine that asks nothing real can m: "A machine that asks nothing real can measure nothing real. Fix the question first." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 2 · Episode 1: The Questi: completed Unit 2 · Episode 1: The Question Machine. They showed mastery of statistical questions and histograms.
map.Thank you for reading with the crew. Epi: Thank you for reading with the crew. Episode 2 waits in the middle of everything.
map.A different poster asks: 'How many seeds: A new poster asks: 'How many seeds are in each festival pumpkin?' Seed counts change from pumpkin to pumpkin → statistical.
map.'How many letters are in the word FESTIV: 'How many letters are in the word FESTIVAL?' One fixed count, no matter who counts → NOT statistical.
map.The test is variability — not whether th: The test is variability, not whether the answer is a number. Both answers are numbers. Only one varies.
map.A form has 5 questions; 2 of them have a: A form has 5 questions. 2 of them have answers that vary. How many are statistical?
map.Different log — minutes at the face-pain: A new log, minutes at the face-paint booth: 3, 11, 7, 14, 2, 9, 12, 6. Bins: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14.
map.Tick each value: 0–4 gets 3, 2 → height: Tick each value: 0–4 gets 3, 2 → height 2. 5–9 gets 7, 9, 6 → height 3. 10–14 gets 11, 14, 12 → height 3.
map.Check the total: 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 values. A: Check the total: 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 values. All the data is counted, with no gaps between bars.
map.In that worked log, how tall is the 5–9: In that worked log, how tall is the 5–9 bar?
map.Different board: 10 readings in bins of: A new board: 10 readings in bins of 2, 5 and 3. Where is the middle pair, the 5th and 6th readings?
map.Count up in order: bin one holds reading: Count up in order: bin one holds readings #1–2. Bin two holds readings #3–7. So the 5th AND 6th both land in bin two.
map.Count for 'bin two or higher': 5 + 3 = 8: Count for 'bin two or higher': 5 + 3 = 8 readings. The bars never forget how many.
map.On that board (bins 2, 5, 3), how many r: On that board (bins 2, 5, 3), how many readings are in the LAST bin alone?
map.Tag all four questions first — every lin: Tag all four questions first. Every line on the form.
map.Sorted! Churros bought and minutes waite: Sorted! Churros bought and minutes waited vary from visitor to visitor. Those can measure the festival. The founding year and the gate count are single facts. Pimm's machine asked half its questions to a sign.
map.All 18 waits stacked — and the festival': All 18 waits stacked. The festival's wait times finally have a shape Pimm can't argue with.
map.Pick a bin for Lock 1 first — Pimm is ta: Pick a bin for Lock 1 first. Pimm is tapping his pen.
map.Lock 1 holds. The first bar holds only 3: Lock 1 holds. The first bar holds only 3 waits: positions #1, #2 and #3. Can the 9th wait fit in there?
map.Lock 1 holds. Count up in order: how man: Lock 1 holds. Count up in order. How many waits come BEFORE the 20–29 bar even starts?
map.Lock 1 holds. A histogram hides the exac: Lock 1 holds. A histogram hides the exact values, but it still COUNTS in order. The first bar covers positions #1–3. Where does the count go next?
map.Lock 2 holds. Two bars cover 'ten minute: Lock 2 holds. Two bars cover 'ten minutes or more'. Add their heights.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Positions #4–11 fill the: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Positions #4–11 fill the 10–19 bin, so the middle pair, 9th and 10th, are both there. And 8 + 7 = 15 waits run ten minutes or more. The Question Machine is out of order!
